svg.title: iOS · Interval grading viewer · keyframed · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift with App/GradeTimelineView.swift between the media and the controls, and App/PhotoAdjustmentsPanel.swift showing keyframed-slider treatment A. The strip is drawn ONLY for a capture with length to grade across — an interval shoot with more than one frame (`hasTimeline`). A Photo-mode capture is one still, has no second moment to grade, and gets exactly the screen project-photo.viewer.portrait.svg draws. Staged by LL_KEYFRAMES=sunset over LL_VIEWER=1, which writes the three moments this file shows. STRIP GEOMETRY (GradeTimelineView's metrics table): 30pt play control, 12pt gap, then the track — a 3pt rail at 18% primary, an 11pt amber moment with a 2pt #C36A00 ring, a 3×22pt playhead in primary UNDER the moments (so a moment the playhead stands on reads as one mark), and the travelling elapsed-time bubble held between 7% and 93% of the track so it never hangs off the end. FRAME STEPS: two 30pt controls in the strip's own idiom (#1C1C1E disc, accent chevron.left/chevron.right) sit after the track, 8pt apart, and take their width out of the track rather than out of the margins — the play control, the track and the steps are one row of transport. Each moves the playhead exactly ONE frame index and re-renders the still the way a finished scrub does; a 0…1 scrubber puts frame 2 of a 250-frame shoot four thousandths along the track, which no thumb can hit. A step that would fall off either end is disabled and its chevron drops to secondary at 45%. They exist only where the strip does (`hasTimeline`) — a Photo-mode capture has no second frame to step to. Head and tail labels are elapsed CAPTURE time, from the frames.timestamps sidecar; the format is chosen from the whole span, so a 2 h 14 min shoot reads h:mm:ss at both ends rather than 0:00 beside 2:14:00. Total strip height is fixed at 45pt (30 + 2 + 13), so the media above it never moves when a moment is added, selected or long-pressed. HIDE BAD FRAMES (staged here, drawn below the fold): this shoot has 2 of its 60 frames nominated bad and hidden, which is why the marquee reads 58 — but the control that does it is deliberately NOT in this part of the screen. Presets, sliders and keyframes are the work; the bad-frame pair — the ⚠ "Mark frame as bad" row and a "Hide bad frames" switch directly under it — sits LAST in the scrolling control stack, past Save as Preset, where somebody who never nominates a frame never meets it. Nothing about nomination appears between the picture and the sliders, and the strip's height is unchanged by any of it (still a fixed 45pt). The switch is a card row in the same idiom as the ⚠ row above it: 15pt title, a 12pt secondary caption that counts what is happening ("2 marked frames are off the timeline and out of this project's counts" / "…stay on the timeline, ticked in orange"), #FFB340 tint, .checkbox style on macOS. Drawn ONLY when there are nominations (`hasNominatedFrames`), and ON by default: a frame marked bad and still in the way is not what the nomination was for. THE AXIS FOLLOWS THE STRIP, NOT THE DISK: hidden frames are not in the scrubber's array at all — the playhead cannot stand on one and the ‹ › steps walk past them — and the clock is rebased onto the first frame the strip actually holds, so hiding the opening two frames of a 4:09 shoot leaves a strip reading 0:00 → 4:07 rather than 0:02 → 4:09. Frames hidden out of the MIDDLE, which is the case drawn here, take no time off either end: the shoot still spans 2:14:00, the strip just steps over those moments, so both end labels stand. A shoot with no per-frame clock scales its recorded duration by the share of frames still on the strip, on the same even-spacing assumption that axis is already built on. With hiding on the strip draws NO bad-frame ticks — there is no position left to mark. Off, the frames come back and the ticks with them: 2×6pt #FF9F0A dashes on a 6pt row under the track, one per nomination, at the frame's own fraction of the track (specified, never yet drawn). `hasNominatedFrames` is measured against the UNFILTERED shoot, so a run where every frame has been nominated keeps the switch after the strip itself has gone — otherwise hiding would be a one-way door with nothing left on screen to undo it. The ⚠ row is untouched by all of this: with hiding on it can only ever say "Mark frame as bad", because a nominated frame is not a frame this screen can reach. STATES NOT DRAWN HERE, all from the same component: SNAPPED — tapping a moment lands the playhead exactly on it and the dot swells to 15pt, swapping its ring for white inside a 1.5pt #C36A00 halo; that is the only “selected” state the screen has, and while it holds, the sliders edit THAT moment rather than making a new one. LONG-PRESS — 550ms on a moment raises a #2B2B2E bubble with “Delete Keyframe” in #FF6B5E and a caret pointing at it; a press that starts on a moment never scrubs, so the moment being aimed at cannot slide out from under the finger. SPARSE vs DENSE — keyframe density is the only speed control there is (ease-in-out is fixed, and there is no curve editor anywhere): a pair an hour apart is a sunset drifting, a pair a few frames apart is a tram going past. PANEL: a property that travels carries the amber diamond (7pt, rotated 45°, #FFB340 on a #C36A00 hairline) beside its label and an accent readout — the readout is then a value at THIS moment, not a value for the clip, which is worth saying even when the number happens to be neutral. Contrast has no diamond here because no moment moves it. A section holding a travelling property is never neutral, so its header keeps its accent dot and its Reset. MODEL: the moments are positions in the SOURCE, 0…1 (GradeTimeline) — never in the output, so the speed and warp layers move no keyframe. Between two moments the grade is their smoothstep blend; outside them the nearest one holds. The project's stored PhotoAdjustments stop grading anything and become a mirror of the opening moment, so the card, the thumbnail and a single-still export keep showing the look the clip opens on. A keyframed grade is always Edited: one preset cannot stand for a look that changes, and a chip tapped here writes its values at the playhead rather than flattening the shoot back to one look (Original is the exception — it clears the timeline with everything else).
svg.text: iOS · Interval grading viewer · keyframed · portrait · 393×852 pt
mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift + App/GradeTimelineView.swift — three moments, playhead between the first two, 2 of 60 frames marked bad and hidden · LL_KEYFRAMES=sunset
